points.description: States TRUE (the process may not be scheduled immediately after the interrupt handler finishes).
Justification: the process's time slice (quantum) can expire while the OS is handling the interrupt.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says the scheduler may run or timer expires, without linking to the time slice ending during the interrupt.

points.description: Justification: so after the handler completes, the scheduler picks a different process to run instead of the interrupted one.
points.partial_credit: Half if says another process may run but gives no reason or only a loosely related reason.

rubric.notes: Full marks need TRUE plus a justification that the time slice ends during interrupt handling so a different process is scheduled afterward. Part marks for a vague or half-stated justification (e.g. 'another process may be scheduled' without the time slice reason). If the answer says FALSE or gives no correct justification, give 0 overall, as the question states.
